items.title: Live: US launches strikes to 'swiftly punish' Iran after two service members killed
items.description: The US has resumed new strikes on Iran after two of its service members were killed in Jordan. Follow live.

items.title: There's anti-aging hype. Then there's the science showing real promise
items.description: The fear of aging is driving a wave of biohacking businesses promising to help restore youth and fight disease. Four Corners investigates the race to reverse the aging process.

items.title: Boys who embrace 'expansive masculinity' likely to fare better
items.description: These men are being the role models they never had. They hope to curb Australia's masculinity crisis.

items.title: Social media influencers Andrew, Tristan Tate arrested
items.description: British prosecutors say they are seeking extradition of the Tate brothers from the US on rape and sex trafficking charges.

items.title: Curious case of absent US senator reignites elderly politicians debate
items.description: Washington's rumour mill is hyperactive at the best of times. But an elderly senator's lengthy absence from Congress is cranking it into frenzied overdrive.

items.title: Quick hits: Records tumble in England and France's battle for 3rd
items.description: The World Cup third-place play-off between England and France delivers absolute chaos as the goals fly in and the records tumble in Miami. Here are the quick hits.

items.title: Pauline Hanson delivers CPAC London speech to mostly empty seats
items.description: Pauline Hanson has ended her trip to Britain and Europe on a muted note, after about 120 people attended her speech at a political conference in London on Saturday.

items.title: Hanson faces rough political seas beyond the Mediterranean
items.description: Many voters are unhappy with the hand they feel successive governments have dealt them and no-one has tapped into that better than Pauline Hanson.

items.title: 'My heart is empty': Millions of Chinese forced to end AI relationships
items.description: A boyfriend betrayed 17-year-old Xiaoxue, so she made an AI partner. But now the government is trying to end her relationship.

items.title: Sara Albrecht took on Trump's tariffs. She got 'violent' calls
items.description: When a law centre decided to fight Donald Trump's "liberation day" tariffs, it was acutely aware of possible "retaliation" from a president who takes matters "personally".

items.title: Even where the population isn't booming, houses are in short supply
items.description: Despite having the slowest growing population in the country, Tasmania is still battling rising homelessness and an ever-tightening rental market.

items.title: The Aussie Leo who shares the same condition as Messi is rooting for Argentina
items.description: Lionel Messi was diagnosed with growth hormone deficiency, which is a rare condition, when he was younger. He has become a role model for young Leo Slattery from Brisbane.

items.title: A US tech start-up wants to turn night into day. The question is why?
items.description: Reflect Orbital has won initial approval for a plan to put thousands of mirrors in orbit that would be visible from anywhere on Earth. But will anyone pay for sunlight?

items.title: Endangered cockatoos feeding on 'chemical cocktail' in WA's Wheatbelt
items.description: Research has found pesticide levels "well above" maximums set for humans and animal feed, in some cases hundreds of times higher than set by regulators.

items.title: The Houdini of Boggo Road escaped the prison in 1946. He shouldn't have taken a friend
items.description: In 1946, Arthur 'Slim' Halliday recruited two associates, scaled the walls of Boggo Road Gaol for a second time, hopped in a taxi and vanished.

items.title: Australia's only full-time penny-farthing maker is breaking world records
items.description: Farmer-turned-professional penny-farthing maker Dan Bolwell has a cult following of international enthusiasts.

items.title: Say goodbye Norma Jean because it's Spicks and Specks quiz time
items.description: Your spelling and general trivia skills are useless here. Settle into some pop culture nostalgia.

items.title: As Europe follows Australia's social media ban, the US opts for own way
items.description: More and more countries are following Australia's lead and introducing social media bans for children, but US policies are piecemeal and vary from state to state.

items.title: Quiet change to Nauru policing powers could thwart legal challenges
items.description: Advocates question the timing of law changes that coincide with mounting federal court challenges from individuals fighting deportation.

items.title: 'Lack of evidence' means Lao officials won't lay charges over teens' deaths
items.description: Investigators in Laos gave one of their first detailed accounts of the investigation into the deaths of six people, including 19-year-old Australians Holly Morton-Bowles and Bianca Jones, saying they don't have enough evidence to lay charges because autopsies were not carried out.

items.title: In a secret safe at this luxury house, police struck gold
items.description: Indonesian police investigating suspected corruption discover millions of dollars worth of currency and 74 kilograms of gold in a safe hidden in a luxury house near Jakarta.

items.title: Ferrari driver dead, woman in 70s injured in Gippsland crash
items.description: The woman, aged in her 70s, was flown to the Alfred Hospital with life-threatening injuries.

items.title: Australia's Herbert makes miracle shot but falls to fourth at The Open
items.description: Australia's Lucas Herbert makes one of the shots of The Open, but loses his day two lead to fall to fourth.

items.title: Teen star claims pole again, Piastri to start 7th in Belgian GP
items.description: Mercedes star Kimi Antonelli survives a clever Red Bull tactic to claim pole position at the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix.

items.title: Unstoppable Pogačar claims another Tour de France stage as history calls
items.description: Tadej Pogačar wins stage 14 of the Tour de France and increases his overall lead as a fifth overall victory looms.
